summary: Verified the 'Uncaught runtime error: 401' fix. Zero unhandled promise rejections / pageerror events across no-cookie, invalid-cookie, deep-page direct-load, logout+back, and full login flows. Backend smoke (auth + 13 endpoints) clean. Browser-level 'Failed to load resource: 401' console entries on unauthed initial load are expected Chrome network logs and are NOT the React dev overlay bug being fixed — pageerror count was 0 in every scenario.
passed: Test 1: Fresh context no cookie -> silent redirect to /login, login form visible, 0 pageerrors
Test 2: Invalid access_token cookie -> silent redirect to /login from /units, 0 pageerrors
Test 3: Direct load of /units, /fees, /expenses, /budget, /vendors, /communications, /compliance, /reports all render their *-page testid with 0 errors
Test 4: Logout via sidebar logout-button + browser back button -> stays on /login, 0 pageerrors
Test 5: Login with treasurer@condoassoc.org succeeds, dashboard-page renders, current-user-email matches

Backend: /api/auth/me, /api/units return 401 unauthed; login returns 200 + sets cookie; /api/auth/me, /dashboard/summary, /units, /fees, /expenses, /vendors, /communications all 200 authed; /budget, /compliance, /reports/annual return 422 (missing required query params - expected, not auth issue); /api/auth/logout 200
notes: Two browser console messages of form 'Failed to load resource: ... 401 ()' appear on unauthed initial /api/auth/me — these are emitted by Chromium for any failed network response and cannot be suppressed by app code. They are NOT uncaught exceptions and do NOT trigger the React dev overlay. The user-reported 'Uncaught runtime error 401' (an unhandled promise rejection) was 0 across all 5 tests as measured via page.on('pageerror').
